threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust document engine exposed through a native CLI, PyO3 Python package and CLI, wasm-bindgen browser/Node APIs, an npm CLI, and a Python stdio MCP server. Document bytes pass through package admission, OPC/XML parsing, comparison/editing/rendering, then return as bytes or are published by the host adapter. Native rendering additionally reads installed fonts and persists a font index. Self-update and maintainer publication are separate privileged workflows. Sources: src/lib.rs:7-35, src/lib.rs:96-165, jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:43-49, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21.
assets: Confidential document text, revisions, comments, metadata, embedded media and generated DOCX/PDF/PNG/report artifacts; these are returned to the invoking caller or written to its selected destinations (src/lib.rs:17-29; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:195-217).

Host filesystem authority: native CLI and ordinary Python/npm adapters possess ambient process access; the MCP document I/O capability is an opened root directory (src/publication.rs:146-165,203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111).

Process availability and memory across Rust, Python and WASM consumers. Default admission allows 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and depth 256; comparison allows 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total, with the same entry/depth limits (src/admission.rs:63-100).
Installed executable integrity, release archives/checksums and conditional signing authority (src/update.rs:25-48,198-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-309).

Native font files and persistent font-index.tsv, including cached font paths and temporary index files. Their authority follows host environment and filesystem permissions, independently of the MCP document root (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3095-3107,3156-3165,3213-3229).

Maintainer GitHub release token, conditional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, registry publication credentials and package integrity (.github/workflows/release.yml:234-235,261-309,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919-959,1063-1069).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX -> admission -> OPC/XML: admission checks pre-index budgets, duplicate decoded/case-folded part names, ZIP structural defects, safe names, bounded inflation and XML policy; it does not extract entries to disk (src/admission.rs:439-490,522-575,736-760,788-803). The shared checked ZIP opener applies structural defects independently of higher-level admission (src/opc/archive.rs:34-51).

Raw XML library caller -> DOM: try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing a DOM; infallible parse_xdocument deliberately skips policy and requires caller validation. Attribute defaults are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte names, 64 MiB values and 128 MiB complete start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-57,90-135). Low-level APIs must not inherit guarantees of higher-level admitted entrypoints merely by association.

Caller edit plan -> source snapshot -> candidate: v1 source_sha256 is optional, verified when supplied; every operation resolves against the untouched source, and preview/application share preparation. The native CLI additionally rereads and hashes the named source before first publication and checks output aliases/collisions (src/edit.rs:5-24,97-106,2073-2094; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655,1764-1823). A hash is a freshness/integrity guard, not user authentication.

Native CLI caller -> ambient output paths: publication opens and holds each parent, stages complete bytes in parent/.jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, and commits per file. Existing files require overwrite/force. Set publication is not atomic; partial commits are reported. Ambient publication replaces a destination symlink itself instead of following its referent (src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,421-514; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1764-1823).

MCP stdio client -> document files: --root defaults to cwd, resolves once, and becomes native OutputRoot authority. Path canonicalization is an early diagnostic; actual reads/writes use root-relative cap-std operations. Output paths reject nonportable names and output symlinks, and overwrite defaults false. All tools share this root; read/write annotations are hints rather than separate caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-245,431-462).

Native Markdown -> local image loader: explicit --resource-path overrides the Markdown input's parent, defaulting to '.', and grants that directory's read capability. Percent-decoded URL schemes and resolved paths outside the canonical root are refused; reads use the opened root capability (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2877,2936-2943). npm's adapter rejects resource_path (jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native render -> font filesystem/cache: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides user font locations; otherwise macOS uses HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux uses XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. System/Word font directories and cached face paths are separate ambient reads. Font index precedence is JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX, with empty/off disabling persistence, otherwise parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. Saves use the index path with extension tsv.<pid>.tmp followed by rename. These operations are outside OutputRoot enforcement (src/convert/font.rs:2263-2275,2281-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3095-3107,3156-3165,3183-3189,3213-3229).

Browser host -> WASM executable: default initialization fetches jubarte_wasm_bg.wasm beside the JavaScript module; the caller may supply another module/URL. This is a code-loading capability, distinct from document relationships. Browser/WASM byte APIs do not expose native publication; Python/npm host wrappers separately perform filesystem I/O (jubarte-wasm/npm/web/jubarte_wasm.js:2575-2594; src/lib.rs:163-165; Cargo.toml:150-153).

Explicit self-update caller -> GitHub release -> installed executable: fixed repository jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, platform archive and SHA256SUMS.txt; noninteractive installation requires --yes, while --check only looks up. Selected versions may downgrade. The binary inside the archive is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]; an extracted-binary lstat hook requires a regular file. Current RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so signatures are not enforced. Unix uses tar.gz and Windows zip; extraction/replacement are dependency-owned (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,144-159,198-257,307-320; Cargo.toml:137-148).

Maintainer publication -> public registries/release consumers: v* tag workflow builds binaries and wheels with read-only job permissions, then a distinct contents:write job publishes GitHub assets. ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is exposed only to the signing step, decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN and removed by an EXIT trap. Missing secrets are accepted only while no public keys are committed. Local release.sh separately publishes crates.io jubarte-redlines, npm jubarte-wasm and jubarte-redlines, and PyPI jubarte-redlines using operator credentials after a typed version confirmation unless skipped (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-309,356-369; scripts/release.sh:875-889,919-959,1063-1069).

Developer tooling has separate ambient capabilities: jubarte-rust-inproc accepts COMPARE paths over stdin and directly reads/writes them; it is a benchmark worker, not a root-confined service. The evaluation harness launches configured agent argv in a run directory and new process session with captured stdout/stderr and a timeout; it does not establish an OS sandbox through these subprocess arguments (jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,29-68,91-99; eval/cli-v2-pilot/harness/exec.py:191-222,240-249).

Validated audit qualifications: extension-selected admission misses relationship-selected auxiliary XML; ignored DOCTYPE events differ from permissive DOM declaration boundaries; Markdown drawing dependency graphs have no cycle check. These are retained as separate findings with source evidence, not safe-control assumptions (src/admission.rs:533-569,788-821; src/convert/mod.rs:3480-3497,20768-20795; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-546,660-663; src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs:1397-1408,1964-1974).

Concrete MCP artifact consumers use <root>/<out> or <root>/<out_dir>/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json,redline.pdf,redline-page-NN.png}; rendering writes page-NN.png and render.pdf. Return recipients are the connected client and root filesystem readers, with OutputRoot publication and overwrite=false (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:195-255). Ordinary Python path.write_bytes and Node fs.writeFileSync remain ambient host-selected output operations (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111).

Concrete ambient font resources: macOS scans /System/Library/Fonts[/Supplemental], /Library/Fonts[/Microsoft] and /Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts; cloud families resolve beneath HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts and require one normal path component. Windows system fonts derive from WINDIR else SystemRoot else C:\Windows, plus LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2236,2281-2315,2855-2862). Font index overrides may be relative to process cwd; absent overrides derive parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv, giving HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Linux, APPDATA/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Windows. Absent HOME/APPDATA can disable default paths; index empty/off disables persistence (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3098-3107).

Developer evaluation artifacts resolve to run_dir/stdout.txt, run_dir/stderr.txt and run_dir/task.output_path, and the configured executable inherits process authority. start_new_session and timeout/process-group termination are lifecycle controls, not filesystem/network authorization (eval/cli-v2-pilot/harness/exec.py:191-222,240-249).
attackerCapabilities: A document producer can supply DOCX/legacy DOC/XML, embedded font/image bytes, relationship metadata, text, comments and formatting to an invoking host, without necessarily controlling its filesystem, environment, credentials or process limits (SECURITY.md:38-74; src/admission.rs:439-575).

An MCP client can invoke the registered read and write tools and choose document-relative paths, output paths and overwrite values within the operator-granted root. The root is shared authority, not tenant separation or per-tool approval (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-160,258-277,373-381).

A caller controlling library configuration can deliberately raise InputLimits, omit a v1 source hash, supply an image loader or choose a WASM initialization resource. Such authorized configuration control is not an attacker privilege gain by itself (src/admission.rs:103-144; src/edit.rs:103-106; jubarte-wasm/npm/web/jubarte_wasm.js:2575-2594).

A release-asset attacker would need authority beyond ordinary document input. With the current empty signing key list, replacing both archive and adjacent checksum is outside SHA-256's authenticity protection; this limitation is documented (src/update.rs:44-48; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).

A local actor manipulating native font index/files, publication parents or deployment environment needs corresponding filesystem/environment access. Impact beyond that existing authority requires a separate victim invocation and privilege/readability difference; none is supplied here.
securityObjectives: Refuse malformed or over-budget packages before unbounded package inflation/DOM work; preserve active limits through higher-level consumers; use checked XML APIs for untrusted raw XML (src/admission.rs:439-575; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:119-135; SECURITY.md:54-74).

Document-supplied relationships must not cause arbitrary host reads, network retrieval, macro execution or process execution. Native Markdown local-image access is an explicit, separately confined capability (src/admission.rs:13-22; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2877).

MCP document paths and publications remain under the opened operator root despite pathname replacement; output overwrite requires an explicit parameter (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,448-462).

Apply the plan to its intended source, refuse stale supplied hashes and invalid anchors, and avoid publishing an incomplete staged candidate. Report partial commit/durability outcomes honestly (src/edit.rs:5-24,2073-2094; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1764-1823; src/publication.rs:168-174).

Install only the explicitly selected platform/version through the self-update flow, verify checksums and regular-file extraction, and distinguish conditional signature support from currently enforced authenticity (src/update.rs:91-108,198-257,307-320).

Keep document processing, browser code loading, native cache I/O, MCP file authority, developer subprocess authority and release publication privileges distinct; host process/OS controls remain necessary for resource and credential isolation (SECURITY.md:71-85).
assumptions: No user deployment context, supplied inventory, supplied threat model or knowledge base was provided. This is a read-only architecture review of inspected repository source, not completed vulnerability-audit coverage or runtime verification.

The library provides no user authentication, password storage, encryption or key agreement; no network-facing multi-tenant service or tenant isolation is established by this source (SECURITY.md:84-85). MCP is configured for stdio (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:381).

Input budgets do not guarantee bounded CPU/memory for every transformation; host process limits are explicitly required. Native CLI/Python/npm adapters read complete source files before engine admission (SECURITY.md:71-74; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2742; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-83; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-55).

Documentation discrepancy retained: src/lib.rs:10-11 describes byte functions as using no temporary files, while native rendering can persist font-index.tsv through a tsv.<pid>.tmp file (src/convert/font.rs:3095-3107,3213-3229). The document package pipeline itself remains in memory.

Documentation discrepancy retained: build_server claims tools only touch files under root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-68), while native rendering can read ambient font files and write the independently configured font index outside that root (src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,2637-2652,3095-3107,3156-3165,3213-3229). MCP document path arguments remain capability-confined; broader exploitability is not established.

Documentation discrepancy retained: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 says GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN raise the API budget, but src/update.rs:198-210 configures neither auth_token nor auth_token_from_env. Offline installed self_update 1.3.1 dependency source has auth_token=None by default and an explicit opt-in environment setter; current integration therefore appears anonymous. Dependency anchors: self_update-1.3.1/src/backends/common.rs:1027-1053; self_update-1.3.1/src/backends/github.rs:391-406.

Signing is explicitly staged rather than currently guaranteed: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-80 agrees with RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None (src/update.rs:44-48). Any actual GitHub secret, deployed release signing status, repository branch/tag protection or registry account policy is unknown.

Policy dependency wording is stale relative to source: SECURITY.md:89-94 names rdocx-opc 0.2/quick-xml 0.41, whereas Cargo.toml uses oxml-opc 0.14.2, quick-xml 0.42 and a separate quick-xml 0.41 alias. This disagreement does not establish an advisory regression; actual resolved dependency behavior needs audit-specific assessment.

Debug is a deliberate unchecked ZIP triage exception, not evidence that normal admission accepts such archives (src/opc/archive.rs:15-19; SECURITY.md:131-136). Raw Relationships::from_xml and infallible DOM parsing have different contracts from admitted document processing (src/opc/mod.rs:45-51; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135; SECURITY.md:92-95).

Font/cache effective paths below are fully derived configuration expressions. No runtime environment, mounted directories, OS ACLs or deployed service account was supplied; a concrete host-specific absolute path cannot be asserted. Browser code origin/CSP and release dependency extraction internals are not fully reviewed.

scope.summary: Independent architecture review of current target; parent-verified core resources. Architecture mapping is not audit-complete file coverage.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX can bypass XML depth limits through auxiliary part names
findings.summary: A crafted DOCX can name a styles, header, footer, or note XML part with a non-.xml/.rels extension. Admission skips its XML policy, but relationship-based rendering parses it recursively. Deep nesting can exhaust the process stack and terminate native consumers or trap WASM execution.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger process availability loss through ordinary rendering APIs without host privileges. Impact is availability of the processing worker, not code execution or data disclosure; deployment-level blast radius is unknown.
severity.changeConditions: Dedicated resource-limited subprocesses reduce impact; a long-lived shared rendering process increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent static trace establishes extension-gated validation, relationship-selected unchecked sinks, and recursion without a depth check. No runtime crash reproduction was executed.

taxonomy.category: XML resource limit bypass / uncontrolled recursion

codeEvidence.label: Admission scans XML by filename suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker chooses the entry name; auxiliary .bin payloads take the non-XML drain branch and never receive check_xml_depth or its shared tag policy.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering performs the incomplete admission first
codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted document bytes reach the renderer and pass admission and bounded package loading; neither normalization nor package loading adds a policy check on non-XML-named auxiliary content.

codeEvidence.label: Relationships select arbitrary auxiliary part names
codeEvidence.explanation: A valid internal styles relationship can select styles.bin; the selection does not require the .xml extension used by the admission gate.

codeEvidence.label: Styles bytes reach unchecked DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The styles string loaded at line 3480 from main_rel_part is forwarded to the permissive parser. With link styles disabled the malicious nesting is unchanged.

codeEvidence.label: DOM parser recurses on each nested element
codeEvidence.explanation: Every attacker-controlled nested opening tag adds a Rust stack frame. This raw parser has no depth limit; skipped admission therefore allows stack exhaustion with a relatively small part.

rootCause.summary: The document supplier controls both auxiliary ZIP names and relationship targets. `admit()` applies `check_xml_depth()` only to .xml/.rels entries and separately the main document part. Rendering selects styles by relationship type via `main_rel_part()`, loads that nonstandard filename, and calls unchecked `parse_xdocument()`. That parser recurses for each nested element, so the filename decision removes the depth guard from the actual parser input. Headers/footers and endnotes use the same unsafe assumption.

findings.remediation: Validate every part that will be interpreted as XML under the active InputLimits regardless of filename. Use checked parsing at auxiliary consumers or identify all XML content types/relationship-selected parts during admission, preserving typed refusal behavior before DOM construction.

counterEvidence: Compressed, inflated-byte and entry-count limits still apply.
The main part is explicitly checked even with an unusual extension.
Markdown Package::xml has its own checked parsing; this finding establishes the conversion path.
SECURITY.md recommends CPU/memory-limited processing; that mitigates blast radius but does not enforce the promised XML depth gate.
limitations: No application execution, crash probe, tests or live deployment inspection.
validation.summary: Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.

dataflow.summary: DOCX ZIP entry + internal relationship -> extension-based admission skip -> PartFs -> main_rel_part -> load_stylesheet -> parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.

impact.why: Stack exhaustion can terminate a native processing worker or trap a WASM call.

likelihood.why: Relationship targets and nested XML are attacker-controlled and require no optional privileged configuration.

reachability.summary: Public byte-based conversion APIs accept caller-provided DOCX. An attacker needs only to supply a document that another user or service renders; no remote service deployment is assumed.
preconditions: Auxiliary relationship selects a non-.xml/.rels payload with nesting beyond the configured depth

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with a normal main document and an internal styles relationship pointing to a non-.xml/.rels part containing excessive nested XML, then request PDF/PNG rendering.

remediationTests: Render a package with a styles relationship to deeply nested styles.bin and assert INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Cover header/footer, notes, diagram and text-box relationship targets with nonstandard extensions and active depth/tag budgets.
Verify valid nonstandard auxiliary filenames continue to render.

findings.title: Converting Markdown can exhaust the stack on cyclic drawing dependencies
findings.summary: An untrusted Markdown drawing payload can encode a dependency cycle. Markdown-to-DOCX assembly recursively materializes the graph without a visited set or depth/work budget, causing nontermination and stack exhaustion from a small input.

severity.rationale: Ordinary untrusted Markdown conversion can terminate a native processing worker or trap WASM. Availability impact is bounded to the process or call; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Resource-limited subprocess isolation reduces service impact; shared long-lived conversion workers increase it.

confidence.rationale: Static trace confirms direct public Markdown input, unconstrained graph deserialization and unconditional recursive revisiting. No runtime reproduction was run.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion in drawing dependency graph

codeEvidence.label: Markdown image destinations decode caller payloads
codeEvidence.explanation: Markdown suppliers can provide a drawing destination directly; success stores the decoded graph for package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded JSON becomes a dependency graph without validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Serde validates JSON shape but not graph acyclicity. Flat vectors of relationships with in-range indices satisfy deserialization even when cyclic.

codeEvidence.label: Materialization begins recursive dependency expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal top-level relationship selects a caller-controlled dependency index and starts dep_part; the only graph check is that the index fits.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency expansion revisits cyclic indices
codeEvidence.explanation: used records output filenames, not dependency indices. An in-range self-edge recursively expands the same dependency before any package caching or termination step can occur.

rootCause.summary: `markdown_to_docx()` reads image destinations and accepts a caller-supplied `drawing:` envelope. `decode()` deserializes its flat dependency vector and `part` indices without graph validation. Package assembly invokes `materialize()`, which follows a top-level index into `dep_part()`. Each nested in-range index recursively invokes `dep_part()` again. The `used` set tracks renamed package files, so it neither detects an active index nor memoizes completed graph nodes; a self-edge never reaches the later byte comparison or package write.

findings.remediation: Validate dependency graphs and budgets at drawing decode/materialization. Reject active-node revisits with a typed conversion error, memoize completed dependency indices, and enforce total dependency, edge, byte and traversal budgets before output assembly.

counterEvidence: MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS bound capture from DOCX, but are not applied by decode and do not prevent even a single-node cycle.
The package byte-equality reuse check at drawing.rs:1998 runs after recursive children and is unreachable for cycles.
limitations: No application execution, crash probe or tests.
validation.summary: Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.

dataflow.summary: Markdown image destination -> decode(base64 JSON) -> Document.drawings -> Relate::drawing -> materialize -> dep_part -> repeated dependency index.

impact.why: Unbounded stack consumption can abort native processing or trap WASM execution.

likelihood.why: The input is accepted by the normal conversion path and a flat JSON graph can express a cycle without violating deserializer nesting bounds.

reachability.summary: Public Rust Markdown conversion accepts strings directly; Python and WASM wrappers call the same conversion. No reference document, external image loader, network or privileged options are required.

attackPath.summary: Supply Markdown containing a drawing envelope whose top-level internal dependency leads to a cycle, then invoke Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.

remediationTests: Assert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle return a typed refusal without stack overflow.
Assert a shared acyclic dependency materializes once and preserves relationships.
Apply decode-side dependency/edge/byte budgets to external Markdown envelopes.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX can bypass XML depth checks through a DOCTYPE parser mismatch
findings.summary: Package admission accepts a DOCTYPE event without examining its internal subset. The later permissive DOM parser skips declarations only through the first greater-than character, so markup inside a quoted declaration becomes recursive element input. A crafted .xml part can therefore exhaust the stack despite passing the XML depth budget.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can abort native rendering or trap WASM through the ordinary public conversion interface. This establishes worker availability loss, not external entity access or code execution.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation limits the failure to one job; shared long-lived consumers increase the availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Source review confirms both parser behaviors, the installed quick-xml 0.42 DTD scanner's quote-aware internal-subset handling, and the renderer's direct unchecked parse after admission. No runtime reproduction was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Admission ignores declaration events
codeEvidence.explanation: The match only counts Start/End events. DocType falls through Ok(_), so nested markup held inside a quoted declaration contributes no admission depth.

codeEvidence.label: DOM declaration skipping ends at the first delimiter
codeEvidence.explanation: The raw parser does not respect quoted declaration contents or the internal subset. Its first delimiter can be inside declaration text, leaving subsequent attacker-controlled opening tags to be parsed as elements.

codeEvidence.label: Misinterpreted markup recurses without a depth guard
codeEvidence.explanation: Remaining nested markup consumes one Rust stack frame per element. The depth guard ran against a different event stream and does not constrain this recursion.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering hands admitted bytes to the permissive parser
codeEvidence.explanation: After with_layout's admission and normalization at lines 773-778, the main part is parsed without checked XML validation. A Transitional input without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting keeps the malicious declaration.

rootCause.summary: The document author controls XML bytes in a normal .xml package part. `check_xml_depth()` relies on quick-xml events and ignores DocType, including its quote-aware internal subset. The next parser uses `index_of(">")` to skip the same declaration and then interprets the remaining markup as ordinary elements. Deep markup contained inside declaration text is invisible to admission's depth counter but drives unbounded `parse_element()` recursion during conversion. The two parsers disagree about the boundary of the same input token.

findings.remediation: Reject DOCTYPE declarations during package admission, consistently with the checked XML API, or replace declaration handling with one parser whose token boundaries and enforced budgets match DOM construction. Enforce recursion limits at the consuming parser as defense in depth.

counterEvidence: The checked raw XML APIs document and enforce DTD refusal, but package conversion uses the permissive parser after a different admission scanner.
No custom entity expansion, external entity resolution or network request is required or claimed.
Archive byte limits still apply and host process limits reduce blast radius.
limitations: No application execution or runtime crash reproduction.
Other operations using admitted XML may share the mismatch, but only the inspected render path is asserted here.
validation.method: independent offline static source and local dependency trace
validation.summary: Verified admission.rs:798-821 has no DocType refusal, parse.rs:539-547 stops at the first delimiter, and parse.rs:660-663 recurses. Installed quick-xml 0.42 source parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205 and reader/state.rs:163-173 show that quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST content is returned within one DocType event. Main-part metadata checks inspect existence/content type rather than XML declaration safety. with_layout then parses the unchanged Transitional main XML.

dataflow.summary: DOCX .xml bytes -> quick-xml DocType ignored by admission -> unchanged part string -> permissive declaration skip -> recursive DOM construction.

impact.why: The worker can exhaust its stack or trap before conversion returns an ordinary error.

likelihood.why: The declaration and its quoted contents are controlled by the document author, and source checks do not reject the discrepancy.

reachability.summary: The public DOCX conversion byte API receives attacker-supplied packages directly. The document need not use unusual filename extensions or enable any optional rendering feature.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX containing quoted nested markup inside an internal DOCTYPE declaration and request rendering. Admission treats the declaration as one ignored event; the later parser treats its remainder as nested elements.

remediationTests: Assert package admission rejects a DOCTYPE internal subset containing quoted markup before any DOM work.
Verify checked raw XML and package conversion agree on declaration refusals.
Cover both normal XML extensions and relationship-selected auxiliary inputs without weakening existing tolerances.

surfaces.label: Auxiliary XML selected by relationships
surfaces.notes: Extension-based gate bypass confirmed at src/admission.rs:533-569; relationship-based styles/header/endnote sinks independently traced. Candidate auxiliary-xml-extension-bypass.

surfaces.label: Markdown drawing dependency graphs
surfaces.notes: Candidate drawing-dependency-cycle independently validated against src/markdown/write.rs:4189, package.rs:1705 and drawing.rs:1964-1974; failed investigator's original evidence preserved in prior checkpoint.

surfaces.label: DOCTYPE handling across package admission and DOM parsing
surfaces.notes: Candidate doctype-parser-depth-differential independently validated by source and installed quick-xml 0.42 scanner; distinct from auxiliary filename coverage because the mismatch occurs inside scanned .xml entries.

surfaces.label: ZIP structural validation
surfaces.notes: Baseline fully audited src/opc/archive.rs and src/opc/zip32.rs: checked opener at archive.rs:34-51 rejects structural defects, header/name/method/flag/CRC/size mismatches, descriptors/overlap and special entries. Debug's unchecked triage mode is an intentional exception, not a production admission bypass. Inflation/XML callers outside these files remain partial.

surfaces.label: MCP filesystem path escape hypothesis
surfaces.notes: Source-backed counterevidence: mcp_server.py:69-108 creates persistent _OutputRoot; publication.rs:155-165 uses held cap-std authority for actual reads and :175-199 for validated writes. Python path resolution is only diagnostic. No arbitrary escape established. All tools share the operator root over stdio, not tenant-separated identities.

surfaces.label: Native Markdown external/local image escape hypothesis
surfaces.notes: Counterevidence at src/bin/jubarte.rs:2815-2870: percent-decode first, reject URL schemes, canonical containment then capability-relative read. Python/WASM default Markdown bindings configure no image loader (jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1206-1218; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:1483-1488). No implicit SSRF or out-of-root image read established.

surfaces.label: Publication atomicity and ambient CLI outputs
surfaces.notes: Focused investigator fully reviewed publication.rs and Node wrapper. Native stages all files and commits each atomically, honestly reporting partial commit/durability; no global rollback promise (publication.rs:168-174,203-225). Node writeFileSync paths at cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111 derive from operator flags/fixed artifact names, so absence of native transactional publication alone is not attacker-controlled arbitrary write. Python direct write helper only mapped, not fully audited.

surfaces.label: Native font filesystem and cache authority
surfaces.notes: Architecture discrepancy verified: lib.rs:10-11 says no temp files and mcp_server.py:67-68 says tools touch only root; font.rs:2637-2652,3098-3107,3156-3165,3213-3229 reads ambient fonts and persists ambient index/temp siblings. Document path confinement still holds. No attacker privilege gain established; font index robustness, local file permissions and all rendering resource paths need fuller review.

surfaces.label: Self-update authenticity and extracted-file type hypothesis
surfaces.notes: Fully audited src/update.rs. Fixed repo/platform/archive path, explicit invocation/confirmation or --yes, checksums and regular-file lstat hook at :198-257,:307-320. Keys=[] and signed threshold=None (:44-48) deliberately select documented checksum-only updates; no attacker control of release channel/TLS or separate key compromise established. Rejecting the finding does not assert signed updates. Dependency extraction remains only mapped, not fully audited.

surfaces.label: Updater documentation and effective API authentication
surfaces.notes: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 promises GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN budget increase; src/update.rs:198-210 uses neither token setter. Installed self_update 1.3.1 default auth_token=None/auth_token_from_env=false at backends/common.rs:1052-1053 supports anonymous configuration. Retain discrepancy; no credential disclosure established.

surfaces.label: Edit snapshot authentication hypothesis
surfaces.notes: V1 source_sha256 is optional and checked when supplied (src/edit.rs:97-106,2073-2094); it is a freshness guard, not caller authentication. Native CLI rechecks source bytes before first commit (src/bin/jubarte.rs:1644-1655,1800-1802). No lower-trust caller authentication bypass established. Full edit-plan logic remains deferred.

surfaces.label: Privileged release and developer subprocess boundaries
surfaces.notes: Mapped and consumer-verified: release.yml:261-309 step-scoped signing secret -> RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN, cleanup; :356-369 job token publishes selected tag. release.sh:875-889,919-959,1063-1069 uses operator publication authority. Evaluation exec.py:191-249 uses configured argv/cwd, stdout/stderr and timeout, not an OS sandbox. No attacker path from document bytes to these privileges established; entire workflows/harness/scripts still require full source audit.

surfaces.label: Embedded credentials and private keys
surfaces.notes: Baseline searched current visible/hidden source, config, documentation, examples/tests for credential formats and private-key headers with no candidate. This is pattern-only evidence; remaining files/archives and generated artifacts were not fully manually examined. No credential was used, copied into the model or sent to a service.

surfaces.label: Remaining authorized current source
surfaces.notes: Current inventory: 2900 tracked/unignored files; union/intersection of baseline, focused and parent fully audited sets: 16 unique files. Architecture-only mapping and excerpts excluded from that count. Exact 2884 unaudited paths retained in deferred task incomplete-baseline-and-focused-review; includes src/admission.rs, src/convert/mod.rs, src/markdown/write.rs, src/markdown/package.rs, src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs, src/bin/jubarte.rs, src/cli.rs and src/opc/mod.rs despite targeted finding validation.

Metadata recovery established 16 fully audited current files out of 2900; the exact 2884 remaining paths are attached. No unvalidated finding remains, but these files require full review, including files viewed only in excerpts and implementation-owning WASM artifacts.

resolved_questions.question: Does the reviewed MCP server expose a network listener?
resolved_questions.disposition: Entrypoint runs MCP over stdio; file operations use native OutputRoot in addition to preliminary containment; native authority not fully reviewed by baseline.

resolved_questions.question: What ZIP structural controls were verified?
resolved_questions.disposition: Shared opener compares local/central names, compression, selected flags, CRC/sizes; checks descriptors/overlaps and special metadata, with checked fields/arithmetic.

resolved_questions.question: Were embedded credentials examined?
resolved_questions.disposition: Offline current visible/hidden source/config/docs/examples/tests common credential/private-key searches produced no candidate. Pattern-based, not full manual review of all files; no use/network.

resolved_questions.question: Can Markdown images escape native resource root?
resolved_questions.disposition: No escape established: percent decoding, scheme rejection, canonical containment and held capability at src/bin/jubarte.rs:2815-2870.

resolved_questions.question: Do Python/WASM Markdown bindings implicitly read host image files?
resolved_questions.disposition: No image loader configured by default; ordinary image references become alt text.

resolved_questions.question: Does MCP enforce its root?
resolved_questions.disposition: Actual I/O routes through persistent native _OutputRoot; Python containment is diagnostic.

resolved_questions.question: Are native publication failures globally rolled back?
resolved_questions.disposition: No global rollback promised; full staging then per-file atomic commits, report already committed paths/uncertain durability.

resolved_questions.question: Does Node CLI provide native publication guarantees?
resolved_questions.disposition: No: writeFileSync and sequential bundles, but reviewed paths are operator/fixed, no document-controlled arbitrary destination established.

resolved_questions.question: Were all Markdown/CLI files fully audited?
resolved_questions.disposition: No: write.rs, package.rs, drawing.rs, bin/jubarte.rs, cli.rs, opc/mod.rs only selected excerpts.

openQuestions: Complete full-file source review for the exact remaining paths in deferred work; broad searches, targeted finding proof and architecture mapping cannot establish complete audit coverage.
Deployment process isolation, memory/CPU limits and shared worker lifecycle are unknown; how widely does a failed conversion affect other jobs?
Native font-index persistence operates outside the MCP document root. Which host paths/permissions are actually configured, and can a distinct lower-privilege actor manipulate its files?
Browser module delivery/CSP, release account protections, signing secret presence and dependency-owned extraction internals were not established.
Review binary DOCX/DOC/font fixtures and implementation-owning generated WASM as data, and finish current-source secret/context review before claiming repository-wide coverage.
